value.rules_markdown:
- Use Rust 2024 idioms with rustfmt output; snake_case modules/files, PascalCase types.
- Return Result<T> using the crate error type from src/error.rs.
- Every file opens with a //! module doc describing its role and feature gating.
- Comments explain the decision, not the code; load-bearing flags/orderings must say why.
- Public items carry doc comments; Clap fields use /// that becomes help text.
- Tests live in-crate: #[cfg(test)] mod tests at end of module, move to test.rs when large. No tests/ directory.
- Every port has an always-compiled offline mock; MockForge records writes for assertions.
- Lane behaviour has golden tests with fixture diff and canned model response.
- Maintain at least 80% coverage for meaningful library behaviour.
- Keep each Markdown file at 500 lines or fewer; split and link when it grows.
- The model never holds a write token; write credentials minted only after all model calls return.
- Contributor code is never executed; we read diff/tree, never build or run target scripts.
- Treat PR bodies, comments, diffs as untrusted input; fence and label them in prompts.
- Secrets found are reported by type and location only; value never reaches comments, check-run summaries, or logs.
- Use concise imperative commit subjects; keep commits small and coherent.
- PRs state what changed, any behaviour change, and how verified.
